title: A handful of personal observations does not test what produced a behavior
summary: OpenStax says limited personal observations and anecdotal evidence cannot rigorously test a hypothesis.
body: OpenStax Psychology says personal observations often suggest a hypothesis, for instance after watching children copy something they just saw. It then says those limited observations and anecdotal evidence cannot rigorously test the hypothesis. A repeated household story is not that test. The point is about evidence. It is not about any named family. A story repeated at home can propose a cause, and the chapter says that repetition is still not a rigorous test.

sources.title: OpenStax Psychology, 2.3 Analyzing Findings
sources.author: OpenStax
sources.note: OpenStax Psychology web page, CC BY 4.0. Paraphrase; credit OpenStax. Supports the contrast between anecdote and a rigorous test of a hypothesis.
